page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by the custom 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture. Powered by ARM Neoverse-V3 cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, the system exposes 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). The processor structure provides 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a unified 48 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning sits at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 34 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and incorporates zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements place the instance among top-tier performers across core CPU and data manipulation tasks. In Geekbench tests, it delivers a single-core score of 2328.0 and a multi-core score of 29666.0, ranking in the top 10 percent alongside notable results in software compilation (103002.0) and ray tracing (92314.0). Multi-core stress-ng throughput reaches 126148.66, falling in the top 25 percent. Data compression benchmarks reflect similar strength, registering 36.35 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 864.39 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. PassMark evaluation highlights high memory and database operation scores of 4704.59 and 58281.8 respectively, alongside a Redis SET rate of 180.55 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 174.71 GB/sec.

The absence of internal NVMe storage requires all persistent disk access to depend on attached network volumes, making network throughput and latency central operational factors. For compute workloads, the 1:2 memory configuration maximizes processing density relative to memory overhead, driving high computational efficiency across ARM-native codebases. CPU-based machine learning inference tests reflect middle-tier throughput—such as 163.84 tokens/sec for medium model prompt processing and 9.71 tokens/sec for text generation—confirming that dense mathematical matrix operations without hardware accelerators face standard architectural constraints.

The c9g.16xlarge instance is suited for compute-heavy parallel applications, large-scale source code compilation, high-throughput web serving, batch compression, and distributed database nodes configured with remote storage.
